overview: Norway is a country in northern Europe, on the western side of the Scandinavian peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Oslo. Norway is a constitutional monarchy and became fully independent from Sweden in 1905. It is not a member of the European Union. Oil and gas from under the North Sea have made it one of the richest countries in the world.

geography.text: Norway is long, narrow and mountainous, with a deeply cut coastline of fjords carved by glaciers. Thousands of islands lie off the coast, and in the far north, beyond the Arctic Circle, the sun does not set in midsummer. The Svalbard islands, far out in the Arctic Ocean, are also part of Norway.

history.text: Norwegian Vikings sailed as far as Iceland, Greenland and North America. Norway was united as a kingdom around the 900s, but from 1380 it was joined with Denmark, and from 1814 with Sweden. It became fully independent in 1905. Occupied by Germany in the Second World War, Norway later grew rich from North Sea oil, discovered in 1969.

events.title: Vikings in America
events.text: Leif Erikson reaches North America, around 500 years before Columbus.

events.title: Constitution
events.text: Norway adopts a constitution, then enters a union with Sweden.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Norway peacefully ends its union with Sweden.

events.title: German invasion
events.text: Germany occupies Norway for five years.

events.title: Oil discovered
events.text: Oil is found under the North Sea, transforming the economy.
